bio: Baptized 'Thomas Toppyn' at Totternhoe, Bedfordshire, 19 Mar 1608/9, son of John. Married Emma Aldridge at Dunstable 16 Nov 1628; eldest son Thomas baptized at Totternhoe 25 Oct 1629. A Wraysbury, Bucks., court roll of 12 Apr 1636 names him one of two overseers reporting that 'all was well with the water courses' (Wraysbury parish contains Magna Carta Island). At Wethersfield, Conn., by 1639 and its deputy to the CT General Court in 1639; Milford 1639/40; then Southampton. 'Topping's Purchase': Indian deeds of 1662 and 1666, paid with 20 fathoms of wampum. Named in King Charles II's 1662 charter for Connecticut — Savage: 'one of the company to whom King Charles granted his letters patent for the Colony of Connecticut' (Conn. Hist. Soc. Coll. 3:306). Married three times. In 1686 deeded his Southampton lands to sons Elnathan and James. Died at Branford, Dec 1687 (1687/8), 'many years a magistrate'. Howell's 1887 'refugee from religious persecution' is family tradition only. Society of Colonial Wars: captain, magistrate, deputy — qualifying, but route depends on Temperance's parentage. Round 1 moved him from 10th to 11th great-grandfather (13 generations). TREE: 'Captain T I Topping 1608–1687 + Emma C Aldridge… 1610–1665 (ship image)', shown as father of John Topping (1636–1686) — that line (John → Josiah → Jerusha) is removed.
